1gdzzta: When someone attributes a mistaken cause to something that did happen, you reject it with «no porque» + subjunctive and give the real cause with «sino porque» + indicative. The action is real; what you deny is the reason. The subjunctive marks that the cause is not accepted. The tense follows the frame: present («no porque falten clientes»), perfect («no porque haya bajado la venta») or imperfect if you are talking about the past («no porque estuviera cansada»).
8oyl1v: Pay attention to the scope of the negation. «No abrió porque estaba enferma» says that she did not open, and why. «Abrió, pero no porque quisiera, sino porque se lo pidieron» says that she opened and denies the reason. With a noun or an infinitive it works the same with «por»: «no por dinero, sino por cansancio»; «no por ser turista, sino por no avisar».

1k1p0m0: «No es que» + subjunctive rejects a possible interpretation; «es que» or «sino que» + indicative give the real explanation. It is very common for softening a refusal: «No es que no quiera ayudarte, es que el sábado trabajo». You can also use it to correct an exaggeration: «No es que el barrio esté mal; es que ha cambiado muy rápido».
1j6dyb7: Causal connectors have a position and a register. «Como» always goes at the start: «Como suben tantos turistas, abrimos antes». «Porque» usually comes after the main idea. «Ya que», «puesto que» and «dado que» present a known cause and are more formal; «debido a» + noun and «a causa de» belong to informative texts. In conversation, after an order, «que» introduces the cause: «Abrígate, que en el cerro corre viento».

sgtb5: Tan, tanto, tal: intensity has consequences
1cenk7e: When a consequence comes from an intensity, the intensity is marked in the first part and the consequence arrives with «que». «Tan» goes before an adjective or an adverb: «la calle es tan empinada que…», «subían tan despacio que…». «Tanto» agrees with the noun: «tanta gente», «tantos cruceros», «tantas mochilas». After a verb, «tanto» does not change: «llovió tanto que…».
1vtmz1l: «Tal» + noun highlights the kind or degree of something: «había tal ruido que no oíamos el timbre», «dijeron tales cosas que nadie volvió». «De tal manera que» or «de tal modo que» refer to the manner: «lo explicó de tal manera que todos lo entendieron». The consequence is in the indicative because it is a fact.
1y7hs5e: Look at the next word: adjective or adverb → «tan»; noun → «tanto» with agreement; nothing (after the verb) → «tanto».

1dokdq2: If the consequence does not depend on an intensity but on a fact, «así que» is enough, and it comes after a comma: «El ascensor estaba cerrado, así que subimos por la escalera». Do not confuse consequence with cause or purpose: «porque» explains what came before, «para que» states the goal and «así que» reports what resulted.
7c41fq: In more formal texts you will find «por lo tanto», «por consiguiente» or «de modo que», with the same value. And when the main sentence is negative, the imagined consequence can go in the subjunctive: «No es tan caro que no puedas pagarlo». For your own writing, remember the basic rule: real consequence, indicative.

1cfa1wz: At eleven on a Sunday morning in February, Templeman street is so full that you have to walk sideways. Groups arrive from the pier, couples with paper maps and students who come up from the flat part of the city with soaking T-shirts. Since the nearest funicular has been under repair for months, almost everyone walks up, so the last stretch turns into a small procession of breathless people.
zvh9dw: The residents tell it without bitterness. «It's not that we're against tourism», explains Ester Valdés, who has lived on the hill for forty years. «It's that the neighbourhood changed so fast that we didn't have time to get used to it». In a decade, half the houses on her block became hostels or souvenir shops, and rents went up so much that several families left for other hills.
1woxcb4: It would be easy to blame the cruise ships, but the explanation is more complex. The ships do not bring so many passengers that the hill cannot receive them; the problem is that almost all of them arrive at the same time and walk along the same four streets. Since the guided tours always follow the same route, there are corners of the hill that get saturated and others, two hundred metres away, where nobody goes all day.
1x4hnri: Local shops are finding their own way to hold out. A bookshop on Almirante Montt street stopped opening on Sundays, not because it was selling little, but because its owners were exhausted. A bakery does the opposite: it opens at six to serve residents before the groups come up. «There are days with such a crowd that we can't even sweep», says its owner, «but in winter, when nobody comes, it's the residents who save us».
woic82: At seven in the evening, when the last group goes down towards the port, the hill gets back some of its silence. You can hear the seagulls and the dogs again.
